claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
The undeformed baseline has a low dislocation density.
The undeformed baseline has a uniform chemical composition.
Applying 10–20% deformation before cooling increases dislocation density.
Pre-cooling deformation creates heterogeneous nucleation sites.
The deformation produces an increased network of dislocations and associated grain boundaries.
Dislocations act as preferential sites for secondary-phase nucleation.
Grain boundaries act as preferential sites for secondary-phase nucleation.
Increased dislocation density lowers the nucleation energy barrier for secondary phases.
Lowering the nucleation barrier accelerates secondary-phase formation during cooling and aging.
Enhanced dislocation density increases the secondary-phase fraction relative to an undeformed sample.
Deformed samples will have a higher secondary-phase volume fraction than the pristine baseline.
Deformed samples will have a finer dispersion of secondary phases than the pristine baseline.
Measured dislocation density will correlate positively with secondary-phase fraction.
Low dislocation density and uniform composition in the undeformed baseline result in limited secondary-phase nucleation.
The defect-mediated mechanism is dominant when local compositional variations are minimized.
Substantial deformation-induced chemical inhomogeneity can drive phase nucleation independently of dislocations.
The proposed mechanism should not apply when substantial chemical segregation independently governs nucleation.

contradictions.description: The alloy is specified as being in its high-temperature BCC state when deformation is introduced before cooling, yet the proposed deformation is described as cold-work. Cold-work normally denotes deformation at relatively low temperature, so the deformation temperature and sequence are internally ambiguous.
